braille.title: Braille Alphabet
braille.intro_text: Welcome to the world of the Braille alphabet, where every letter and number is represented using 6 dots arranged in 2 columns and 3 rows, and counting goes by column (from top to bottom, the first column is 1, 2, and 3, and the second column, in the same order, is 4, 5, and 6 - as shown in the picture). The keyboard letters can also help you: F, D, S = dots 1, 2, and 3 (left hand), J, K, L = dots 4, 5, and 6 (right hand). In other words, for easier orientation, your left hand is for the first column and your right hand for the second; your index finger is for the first, topmost dot in the column (dots 1 and 4), your middle finger is for the second, middle dot in the columns (dots 2 and 5), and your ring finger is for the third, lowest dots in the columns (3 and 6).
braille.mode_compose_desc: Press the correct dots for each letter.
braille.mode_recognize_desc: Listen to the dots and guess the letter/number.
braille.mode_write_desc: Write each letter without a reminder.
braille.mode_word_desc: Listen to the word, then build it dot by dot.
braille.mode_express_desc: Write your own sentences freely, letter by letter.
braille.keyboard_hint: F D S / J K L - dots 1-6  ·  H - pair 2 (for two-pair signs)
braille.word_hint: Spell the word dot by dot (including the capital or number sign, if needed).
braille.express_hint: Press the dots (F D S / J K L), then A to hear the sign. A again confirms. With no dots, A and A = space.
braille.express_empty: Your sentence will appear here once you start writing.
braille.express_keyboard_hint: F D S / J K L - dots  ·  H - pair 2 (for @ and /)  ·  A - speak/confirm (no dots: space)  ·  . ? ! - end of sentence  ·  G - voice command  ·  . - delete dot  ·  : - delete letter  ·  P - reference
braille.express_explanation_text: Here you freely write your own sentences in Braille, sign by sign. You choose the dots with the keys F, D and S (dots 1, 2 and 3) and J, K and L (dots 4, 5 and 6). When you have chosen the dots, press A to hear what you wrote. If it's right, press A once more to confirm it. If only one dot is wrong, delete it with the period key (.); to delete the whole letter, press the colon key (:). If nothing is started, colon deletes the last written sign. For a new word, choose no dots and press A twice - that is a space. The sentence ends when you write a period, question mark or exclamation mark, and then the whole sentence is read back to you. For a capital letter, first write the capital sign (dot 6), then the letter. For a number, first write the number sign (dots 3, 4, 5 and 6); after that the dots are read as digits until the space. The at sign and the slash have two pairs of dots: first you write pair 1, then press H to move to pair 2, and H again takes you back to pair 1. The P key opens the reference, and P again takes you back. You can save your sentence and look at your saved sentences later. The G key turns on the voice command.
braille.sentence_explanation_text: The app tells you a sentence, and you write it in Braille, sign by sign. You can listen to the sentence as many times as you like with "Listen to the sentence", and with "What's next?" you hear the letter or sign that comes next. Writing works just like in "Express Your Thought": choose the dots with F, D and S (dots 1, 2 and 3) and J, K and L (dots 4, 5 and 6), press A to hear the letter, and A again to confirm it. For every correct sign you will hear a success sound. If you write a wrong letter, digit or sign, you will hear a mistake sound right away and can try again. A space is A twice with no dots. Remember: the sentence starts with a capital letter, so first write the capital sign (dot 6), and digits need the number sign first (dots 3, 4, 5 and 6). The sentence ends with a period, question mark or exclamation mark. The period key (.) deletes only the last dot, and the colon key (:) deletes the whole letter. For the at sign and the slash, use the H key for pair 2. The P key opens the reference, and the G key turns on the voice command.
braille.express_no_saved: You haven't saved any sentence yet.
braille.explanation_space: Space - no dots. It goes between words and ends number mode.
braille.explain_capital: Write it before a letter that should be capital.
braille.explain_number_sign: After it, the dots are read as digits until a space.

braille.intro_touch_text: Welcome to the world of the Braille alphabet, where every letter and number is represented using 6 dots arranged in 2 columns and 3 rows, and counting goes by column (from top to bottom, the first column is 1, 2, and 3, and the second column, in the same order, is 4, 5, and 6 - as shown in the picture). On the phone the dots are arranged just like on a braille writer: dots 1, 2 and 3 run along the left edge of the screen (left hand), and dots 4, 5 and 6 along the right edge (right hand). At the top are dots 1 and 4 - for your index fingers, in the middle are dots 2 and 5 - for your middle fingers, and at the bottom are dots 3 and 6 - for your ring fingers. The phone is easiest to use held with both hands or placed on a table in front of you. When you tap a dot, it lights up and the phone vibrates.
braille.express_explanation_touch_text: Here you freely write your own sentences in Braille, sign by sign. You tap the dots on the screen: dots 1, 2 and 3 are on the left, and dots 4, 5 and 6 on the right. When you have chosen the dots, tap the “Speak / confirm” button to hear what you wrote. If it's right, tap it once more to confirm it. If only one dot is wrong, tap “Delete dot”; to delete the whole letter, tap “Delete letter”. If nothing is started, “Delete letter” deletes the last written sign. For a new word, choose no dots and tap “Speak / confirm” twice - that is a space. The sentence ends when you write a period, question mark or exclamation mark, and then the whole sentence is read back to you. For a capital letter, first write the capital sign (dot 6), then the letter. For a number, first write the number sign (dots 3, 4, 5 and 6); after that the dots are read as digits until the space. The at sign and the slash have two pairs of dots: first you write pair 1, then tap “Pair 2” at the top for the second pair, and “Pair 1” takes you back. The “Reference” button shows all the signs. You can save your sentence and look at your saved sentences later. The voice button turns on the voice command.
braille.sentence_explanation_touch_text: The app tells you a sentence, and you write it in Braille, sign by sign. You can listen to the sentence as many times as you like with “Listen to the sentence”, and with “What's next?” you hear the letter or sign that comes next. Writing works just like in “Express Your Thought”: tap the dots on the screen - dots 1, 2 and 3 are on the left, and dots 4, 5 and 6 on the right. Tap “Speak / confirm” to hear the letter, and tap it again to confirm it. For every correct sign you will hear a success sound. If you write a wrong letter, digit or sign, you will hear a mistake sound right away and can try again. A space is “Speak / confirm” twice with no dots. Remember: the sentence starts with a capital letter, so first write the capital sign (dot 6), and digits need the number sign first (dots 3, 4, 5 and 6). The sentence ends with a period, question mark or exclamation mark. “Delete dot” deletes only the last dot, and “Delete letter” the whole letter. For the at sign and the slash, choose “Pair 2” at the top. The “Reference” button shows all the signs, and the voice button turns on the voice command.

picture_book.title: Learn & Listen
picture_book.intro: Educational picture books are available for different topics across several categories. Choose a category and go through all the picture books, where you'll hear something informative about the topic, with the option to also hear what sound it makes. Once you've gone through all the picture books, a quiz follows to test what you've learned. Good luck!
picture_book.quiz_intro_info: Guess which concept the following is about!
picture_book.quiz_result: You finished the quiz with {} out of {} correct!
picture_book.end_of_book: End of book. Well done! Starting from the beginning.
picture_book.long_press_hint: Long press to hear this page again.
picture_book.hint_nav: Swipe left or right for next or previous page. Double tap for next, triple tap for previous.
picture_book.hint_tap: Tap to hear the explanation again.
picture_book.cat_desc: A furry animal that says meow
picture_book.cat_learn: A cat has four legs and sees well in the dark. It catches mice.
picture_book.cat_learn2: When you hear meow outside, it may be a cat. Do not touch unknown animals without permission.
picture_book.dog_learn: The dog is people's loyal friend. It has a strong sense of smell.
picture_book.car_learn: A car moves with an engine. Always cross the street at a crosswalk.
picture_book.rain_learn: Rain waters plants. Wear rain clothes when it is cloudy.
picture_book.sun_learn: The sun gives us light and warmth. Do not look directly at the sun.
picture_book.tree_learn: Trees make oxygen for breathing. They give shelter to animals.
picture_book.bicycle_learn: Cycling is healthy and eco-friendly. Always wear a helmet and follow traffic rules.
picture_book.water_learn: Your body needs water to stay hydrated and focused. Drink water regularly, especially when studying or doing sports.
picture_book.water_learn2: Tap water is healthy to drink. If you feel thirsty, your body is reminding you: drink water.
picture_book.book_desc: Pages with text and pictures to read
picture_book.book_learn: Reading builds knowledge and imagination. Books and audiobooks are for everyone.
picture_book.fire_desc: Flames that give heat and light
picture_book.fire_learn: Never play with fire. In a fire, get out right away and call emergency 112.
picture_book.fire_learn2: If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll. Call for help.
picture_book.phone_learn: Use the phone to stay in touch and in emergencies. Call 112 for emergency, or your local police and fire numbers.
picture_book.phone_learn2: Remember: 112 emergency. Call only when there is real danger. Say your name and where you are.
picture_book.bird_desc: A small animal that flies and sings
picture_book.bird_learn: A bird flies with wings and sings beautiful songs.
picture_book.cow_desc: A farm animal that gives milk
picture_book.cow_learn: A cow gives milk and eats grass in the meadow.
picture_book.wind_desc: Moving air we feel on our skin
picture_book.wind_learn: Wind is moving air. It can be a gentle breeze or a strong storm.
picture_book.clock_desc: A device that shows the time
picture_book.clock_learn: A clock tells us what time it is, so we can be on time.
picture_book.star_desc: A bright point of light in the night sky
picture_book.star_learn: Stars are huge balls of light far away in space. The Sun is a star too.
picture_book.moon_desc: A bright object that shines at night
picture_book.moon_learn: The Moon orbits the Earth, and we see it as a bright ball at night.
picture_book.rocket_desc: A vehicle that flies into space
picture_book.rocket_learn: A rocket flies very fast to carry people and equipment into space.
picture_book.planet_desc: A big ball that orbits a star
picture_book.planet_learn: Earth is a planet we live on. There are many other planets in space.
picture_book.drum_learn: A drum is hit with hands or sticks to make a rhythm.
picture_book.guitar_learn: A guitar has strings that vibrate when plucked, making beautiful music.
picture_book.bell_learn: A bell makes a clear sound when it's shaken or struck.
picture_book.quiz_info_intro: What is the following characteristic of:
picture_book.grid_hint: Tap a card to open its picture book page. Once you've opened them all, a quiz follows.
picture_book.dog_quiz_desc: A pet that is people's loyal friend and has a strong sense of smell.
picture_book.bird_quiz_desc: A small animal that flies and sings.
picture_book.cow_quiz_desc: A farm animal that gives milk.
picture_book.rain_quiz_desc: Drops of water falling from the sky.
picture_book.water_quiz_desc: We need it to stay hydrated and focused.
picture_book.fire_quiz_desc: It can burn down houses and forests.
picture_book.wind_quiz_desc: Moving air that can be a gentle breeze or a strong storm.
picture_book.car_quiz_desc: It has four wheels and must stop at a crosswalk.
picture_book.bicycle_quiz_desc: Riding it is healthy and eco-friendly. It has two wheels and moves with pedals.
picture_book.star_quiz_desc: Huge balls of light far away in space.
picture_book.moon_quiz_desc: We see it as a bright ball at night.
picture_book.rocket_quiz_desc: A vehicle that flies into space.
picture_book.planet_quiz_desc: A big ball that goes around a star.
picture_book.drum_quiz_desc: You hit it with your hands or sticks to make a rhythm.
picture_book.bell_quiz_desc: A small object that rings when you shake or hit it.
picture_book.quiz_answer_now: Tap the answer or say it out loud!
picture_book.horse_desc: A big, fast animal that neighs
picture_book.horse_quiz_desc: A big, fast animal that neighs.
picture_book.horse_learn: A horse has strong legs and hard hooves. It loves to eat hay, oats and apples.
picture_book.sheep_desc: A farm animal with soft wool that says baa
picture_book.sheep_quiz_desc: A farm animal with soft wool that says baa.
picture_book.sheep_learn: Sheep wool is used to make warm sweaters and socks. Sheep live together in a flock.
picture_book.pig_desc: A pink farm animal with a snout that says oink
picture_book.pig_quiz_desc: A pink farm animal with a snout that says oink.
picture_book.pig_learn: A pig digs in the ground with its snout to find food. When it is hot, it rolls in mud to cool down.
picture_book.duck_desc: A bird that swims and says quack-quack
picture_book.duck_quiz_desc: A bird that swims and says quack-quack.
picture_book.duck_learn: A duck has webbed feet, so it swims very well. Its feathers stay dry in the water.
picture_book.frog_desc: A small green animal that jumps and croaks
picture_book.frog_quiz_desc: A small green animal that jumps and croaks.
picture_book.frog_learn: A frog lives both in water and on land. It catches flies with its long, sticky tongue.
picture_book.rooster_desc: A farm bird that crows cock-a-doodle-doo in the morning
picture_book.rooster_quiz_desc: A farm bird that crows cock-a-doodle-doo in the morning.
picture_book.rooster_learn: A rooster crows early in the morning and wakes people up. It lives in a henhouse with the hens.
picture_book.thunder_desc: A loud rumble in the sky during a storm
picture_book.thunder_quiz_desc: A loud rumble in the sky during a storm.
picture_book.thunder_learn: We see the lightning first and hear the thunder later, because light travels faster than sound.
picture_book.snow_desc: Soft white flakes that fall in winter
picture_book.snow_quiz_desc: Soft white flakes that fall in winter.
picture_book.snow_learn: Snow is frozen water. Every snowflake has six points and is different from all the others.
picture_book.flower_desc: A colorful part of a plant that smells nice
picture_book.flower_quiz_desc: A colorful part of a plant that smells nice.
picture_book.flower_learn: Bees fly from flower to flower to collect nectar for honey. Later, fruits grow from flowers.
picture_book.sea_desc: A big body of salty water with splashing waves
picture_book.sea_quiz_desc: A big body of salty water with splashing waves.
picture_book.sea_learn: Fish, crabs and dolphins live in the sea. Seas and oceans cover most of the Earth.
picture_book.sea_learn2: Swim only with an adult and only where there is a lifeguard.
picture_book.door_desc: We open and close it to go into a house or a room
picture_book.door_quiz_desc: We open and close it to go into a house or a room.
picture_book.door_learn: A door can creak when it opens. Before you enter someone else's room, knock first.
picture_book.door_learn2: Do not open the door to strangers. Call an adult first.
picture_book.key_desc: A small metal object that unlocks a door
picture_book.key_quiz_desc: A small metal object that unlocks a door.
picture_book.key_learn: Every key has its own special teeth and opens only its own lock.
picture_book.key_learn2: Keep your house key in a safe place and do not show it to strangers.
picture_book.scissors_desc: A tool with two sharp blades for cutting paper
picture_book.scissors_quiz_desc: A tool with two sharp blades for cutting paper.
picture_book.scissors_learn: Scissors cut when their two blades slide past each other. There are also children's scissors with rounded tips.
picture_book.scissors_learn2: Carry scissors with the points facing down and use them only with an adult.
picture_book.toothbrush_desc: We use it with toothpaste every morning and evening to clean our mouth
picture_book.toothbrush_quiz_desc: We use it with toothpaste every morning and evening to clean our mouth.
picture_book.toothbrush_learn: Brush your teeth twice a day, in the morning and in the evening, for two minutes. This keeps your teeth healthy.
picture_book.glass_desc: A cup we drink water or milk from
picture_book.glass_quiz_desc: A cup we drink water or milk from.
picture_book.glass_learn: A glass can be made of glass or plastic. Hold a glass cup carefully so it does not break.
picture_book.earth_desc: The blue planet we live on
picture_book.earth_quiz_desc: The blue planet we live on.
picture_book.earth_learn: The Earth goes around the Sun once every year. It is the only planet we know that has life.
picture_book.astronaut_desc: A person who travels into space in a special suit
picture_book.astronaut_quiz_desc: A person who travels into space in a special suit.
picture_book.astronaut_learn: An astronaut wears a spacesuit with air to breathe. In space, astronauts float like feathers.
picture_book.comet_desc: An icy space object with a long bright tail
picture_book.comet_quiz_desc: An icy space object with a long bright tail.
picture_book.comet_learn: A comet is made of ice, dust and rock. When it comes close to the Sun, it grows a bright tail.
picture_book.satellite_desc: A machine that circles the Earth and sends signals
picture_book.satellite_quiz_desc: A machine that circles the Earth and sends signals.
picture_book.satellite_learn: Satellites help us watch TV, check the weather forecast and find our way.
picture_book.ufo_desc: A flying saucer from stories about aliens
picture_book.ufo_quiz_desc: A flying saucer from stories about aliens.
picture_book.ufo_learn: These letters stand for unidentified flying object. In stories and cartoons, aliens travel in it.
picture_book.telescope_desc: A tool for looking at faraway stars and planets
picture_book.telescope_quiz_desc: A tool for looking at faraway stars and planets.
picture_book.telescope_learn: A telescope makes faraway things look close. Scientists use it to explore space.
picture_book.piano_desc: A big musical instrument with black and white keys
picture_book.piano_quiz_desc: A big musical instrument with black and white keys.
picture_book.piano_learn: When you press a key, a small hammer hits a string and makes a note. A piano has 88 keys.
picture_book.violin_desc: A small wooden instrument with strings, played with a bow
picture_book.violin_quiz_desc: A small wooden instrument with strings, played with a bow.
picture_book.violin_learn: A violin is held under the chin. When the bow slides across the strings, it sings softly.
picture_book.trumpet_desc: A shiny metal instrument you blow into loudly
picture_book.trumpet_quiz_desc: A shiny metal instrument you blow into loudly.
picture_book.trumpet_learn: The player buzzes their lips while blowing and changes the notes with three buttons.
picture_book.saxophone_desc: A curved golden instrument you blow into, loved in jazz music
picture_book.saxophone_quiz_desc: A curved golden instrument you blow into, loved in jazz music.
picture_book.saxophone_learn: The saxophone was invented by Adolphe Sax. It is made of metal, but a small piece of reed makes its sound.
picture_book.accordion_desc: An instrument with keys and bellows that squeeze and stretch
picture_book.accordion_quiz_desc: An instrument with keys and bellows that squeeze and stretch.
picture_book.accordion_learn: An accordion plays when its bellows pull in and push out air. It is often played at weddings and folk celebrations.
picture_book.banjo_desc: A string instrument with a round body like a little drum
picture_book.banjo_quiz_desc: A string instrument with a round body like a little drum.
picture_book.banjo_learn: A banjo has a bright, cheerful sound. It is most often played in American country music.
picture_book.microphone_desc: A device we sing or talk into so we can be heard louder
picture_book.microphone_quiz_desc: A device we sing or talk into so we can be heard louder.
picture_book.microphone_learn: A microphone catches our voice and sends it to the speakers. Singers use it at concerts.

number_games.title: Number Games
number_games.what_number: What number is this? Enter it with the keyboard or tap the digits.
number_games.question: What is {}?
number_games.choose_answer: Choose your answer or enter with the keyboard.
number_games.how_many_shapes: How many shapes are there? Listen to the sounds or slide your finger over the shapes, count them and enter the number.
number_games.explanation_text: Choose a difficulty and one of the eight number games. Each round has 10 questions. The questions are spoken aloud, and in the new games you can repeat them with the Repeat button. Answer with the keypad or by touch. After each answer you see a big correct or incorrect sign and hear a sound.

number_games.what_number_touch: What number is this? Tap the digits or say it out loud.

number_extra.explanation_tally: Big circles are scattered across the screen. Slide your finger over each circle - when you touch one you'll hear a number and feel a vibration. The last number you hear is how many circles there are. At the bottom, choose the correct number. The game has 10 rounds.
number_extra.explanation_grid: The screen is divided into squares with numbers. The game tells you which number to find and where on the screen it is. Move your finger across the squares - each square says its number, and when you find the right one you'll feel a special vibration rhythm. The game has 10 rounds.
number_extra.explanation_sequence: A sequence of numbers is shown with one empty spot. Figure out the rule of the sequence. Swipe your finger up or down on the big card to change the number - each number is spoken. When you reach the right number, press Confirm. The game has 10 rounds.
number_extra.explanation_sort: Put the numbers in order from smallest (top) to largest (bottom). Touch a number to hear it, and drag it to move it. Every move makes a click and a vibration. When you're done, press Confirm. The game has 10 rounds.
number_extra.prompt_tally: Touch all the circles, then choose how many there are.
number_extra.prompt_sequence: Which number is missing? Swipe up or down and confirm.
number_extra.prompt_sort: Put the numbers in order from smallest to largest.
number_extra.explanation_sudoku: The board has 9 boxes (top 1 2 3, middle 4 5 6, bottom 7 8 9), each with 9 cells. Every row, every column and every box must contain all the numbers from 1 to 9. The same number must not repeat in the same row, in the same column, or in the same box. The arrow keys ← → ↑ ↓ change the box, and the number keys on the right of the keyboard (7 8 9 top, 4 5 6 middle, 1 2 3 bottom) pick the cell in the box. Enter a number with the number keys at the top of the keyboard, the buttons on the screen, your voice (e.g. "seven" or "box five") or Braille. A wrong number is not written and counts as a mistake.
number_extra.explanation_sudoku_touch: The board has 9 boxes (top 1 2 3, middle 4 5 6, bottom 7 8 9), each with 9 cells. Every row, every column and every box must contain all the numbers from 1 to 9. The same number must not repeat in the same row, in the same column, or in the same box. Tap the cell you want to fill - you will hear which box it is in and whether it is empty. Enter a number with the number buttons below the board, your voice (e.g. "seven" or "box five") or Braille. A wrong number is not written and counts as a mistake.

spatial.title: Spatial orientation
spatial.explanation_simon_text: This game trains spatial memory through touch. First tap 'Start sensing' - you'll feel a sequence of vibrations, each direction (up, down, left, right) with its own distinct pattern. Count and remember them carefully, in order. Then, on the cross-shaped pad below, tap the same directions in the same order you felt them. If you want to feel the sequence again before answering, tap 'Sense again'. Each round adds one more step to the sequence - the game has 10 rounds in total.
spatial.explanation_maze_text: This game trains following an invisible path using only touch and vibration. Tap 'Start maze', then place your finger anywhere on the grid below and slowly move it. While your finger is on the correct path, you'll feel a light, short vibration. As soon as you step off the path (hit a 'wall'), you'll feel a stronger vibration and the border will flash red - go back to the last correct spot and keep searching from there. You must trace the path in order, from the start (green square) to the end (gold square) - you can't skip straight to the end. The game has 5 different mazes.
spatial.explanation_radar_text: This game trains finding a hidden object in space. Move your finger across the whole field - the vibrations get more frequent and stronger the closer you get to the hidden object, like a metal detector. At the start, you'll also see a faint glowing circle around the hidden object's location as a visual aid, but that circle becomes less and less visible from round to round, until by the end you'll need to rely on vibration alone. Once you find the object, a key icon appears - drag the key to the lock in the top-right corner to finish the round. The game has 10 rounds.
spatial.explanation_compass_text: This game trains orientation using the cardinal directions. On a phone with a compass sensor: the game tells you a direction (for example 'North'), and you physically turn around in the room until you're facing that way - once you're close enough, you'll feel short vibrations and a circular progress ring will fill up until it's confirmed. On a computer, instead of physically turning, the game shows an icon that moves and rotates through a specific sequence of steps (up, down, left, right, rotate left, rotate right, stay) - watch it carefully, then use the buttons below to repeat the same sequence so the icon ends up in the same final position.
spatial.coming_soon_maze: Virtual maze: trace a path with your finger through an invisible grid - vibration warns you when you leave the path.
spatial.coming_soon_radar: Digital radar: find a hidden object on the screen by following vibrations that get stronger as you get closer.
spatial.coming_soon_compass: Compass and directions: use your phone's compass to find north, south, east and west.

cyber.question1: Should you share your personal information online?
cyber.explanation1: Never share personal information like your address, phone number, or password online. Always ask a parent or teacher first.
cyber.question2: What should you do if a stranger messages you?
cyber.option2b: Tell a parent or teacher and don't reply
cyber.explanation2: If a stranger messages you online, never reply. Always tell a parent or teacher immediately.
cyber.question3: Is it okay to meet someone you met online in person?
cyber.option3a: No, never meet strangers from online
cyber.option3c: Only if they are your age
cyber.explanation3: Never meet someone you met online in person without a parent or teacher present. It's not safe.
cyber.question4: What should you do if someone is being mean to you online?
cyber.option4b: Tell a parent or teacher and block them
cyber.explanation4: If someone is being mean or bullying you online, tell a parent or teacher right away and block that person.

cyber.explanation_text: Choose one of the cyber safety games. In "Wolf in Sheep's Clothing" you read messages and decide if they're safe or dangerous. In the Quiz you answer questions about internet safety.
cyber.intro_phishing: You will get messages from different people. Say whether each message is safe or dangerous – the wolf in sheep's clothing hides behind friendly words!
cyber.intro_quiz: You will hear questions about staying safe online, each with three possible answers. Pick the right one after you hear them all.
cyber.intro_castle: A password is like a castle wall: the stronger it is, the harder it is to break. Add lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers and symbols to build a strong castle.
cyber.intro_agent: Strangers will ask you personal things. You are a secret agent – decide whether to answer, or to refuse and tell a parent.
cyber.voice_hint_quiz: You can also say: answer “1”, “2” or “3”, “repeat”, “continue”.

pong.title: Voice Pong
pong.explanation_text: Drag your finger up or down in the dark area to move the paddle. The ball bounces off the top, bottom, and right walls - each bounce plays a tick sound that pans in stereo from the right ear to the left. If the paddle intercepts the ball on the left, that's a hit and the ball speeds up each time. If the ball gets past the paddle - the game ends. Try to get as many hits as you can!
pong.final_summary_survival: You got {} hits before you missed!

melody.explanation_text: The game has 20 rounds in total. You will hear a sequence of sounds, one after another - for example cat, cat, dog, car. First tap Start listening. Then tap the same sounds below in the same order you heard them. Each round can have more sounds in the sequence - from 2 up to 7. At the end you'll see how many rounds you got right and how many wrong.

rhythm.explanation_text: The game has 10 rounds in total. Tap Play sound to hear the rhythm and carefully count how many beats you heard. If you want to hear it again, tap Play sound again. Then, in the box below, type the number you think is correct, and tap Confirm. If it matches the real number of beats - correct! At the end you'll see how many rounds you got right.

rhythm.voice_hint: You can also use your voice: say the number (e.g. "seven"), then "confirm". You can also say "play", "play again" or "clear".
rhythm.helper_explanation: Tap the drum for each beat you hear - the number in the box goes up by itself.
rhythm.entry_explanation: This shows the number of beats - you can change it by hand, or press Confirm when you're sure.

story.explanation_text: Listen to the story - it's always shown on screen too. After each story you have two choices; tap the one you like. You'll hear and see what happens next. When you're ready, tap 'Continue' for the next story - no rushing.
story.intro: Story – your choice. Listen and choose what happens.
story.s1_text: Anna goes to the park. She sees a big tree and a swing. Should she swing or pick flowers?
story.s1_out1: Anna swung and smiled. The air was fresh and it was a lovely day.
story.s1_out2: Anna picked pretty flowers and gave them to Mom. Mom was very happy.
story.s2_text: Mark is thirsty. Should he get water from the fountain or look for juice?
story.s2_out1: Mark drank water and felt better right away. Water is the healthiest.
story.s2_out2: Mark found juice and shared it with his friend. Both were happy.
story.s3_text: Sonia wants to read a book. Should she get a book about animals or about space?
story.s3_out1: Sonia read about lions and elephants. She wanted to see them at the zoo.
story.s3_out2: Sonia read about stars and planets. She wanted to become an astronaut.
